note: Review-only file, not for insertion into TestsData. Correct-option rationales included; technical/distractor editorial check remains recommended.

questions.text: What does WWW stand for?
questions.rationale: WWW stands for World Wide Web.

questions.text: Which identifies a website's human-readable name, such as example.com?
questions.rationale: A domain name is a human-readable Internet name.

questions.text: Which protocol is primarily used to transfer web pages between browser and server?
questions.rationale: HTTP is the Web's request/response protocol.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of HTTPS compared with HTTP?

options.label: B
options.text: It encrypts and authenticates the connection using TLS

options.label: D
options.text: It transfers files only over USB

questions.rationale: HTTPS protects HTTP communication using TLS.

questions.text: Which is an example of an IP address?
questions.rationale: The dotted numeric form is an IPv4 address.

questions.text: Which protocol is commonly used for transferring files between systems?
questions.rationale: FTP means File Transfer Protocol.

questions.text: What does a web server primarily do?

options.label: C
options.text: Respond to requests for web resources

options.label: D
options.text: Convert every domain into an image

questions.rationale: A web server serves resources in response to client requests.

questions.text: Which protocol family underpins communication between Internet-connected systems?
questions.rationale: TCP/IP refers to core Internet communication protocols.

questions.text: Which address version uses 128-bit addresses?
questions.rationale: IPv6 uses 128-bit addressing.

questions.text: Which transport protocol is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery?
questions.rationale: UDP is connectionless and provides no delivery guarantee.

questions.text: Which declaration identifies an HTML5 document?
questions.rationale: The HTML5 doctype is <!DOCTYPE html>.

questions.text: Which is the usual outermost element of an HTML document?
questions.rationale: The html element contains the document's head and body.

questions.text: Which element contains metadata and links to stylesheets?
questions.rationale: The head contains metadata and linked resources.

questions.text: Which element sets the title commonly shown in a browser tab?
questions.rationale: The title element specifies the document title.

questions.text: Which element represents a paragraph?
questions.rationale: The p element represents a paragraph.

questions.text: Which element is typically used for the main visible top-level heading?
questions.rationale: h1 is the highest-level heading element.

questions.text: Which element embeds an image into a webpage?
questions.rationale: The img element embeds an image resource.

questions.text: Which attribute of an img element provides alternative text?
questions.rationale: alt provides a text alternative for the image.

questions.text: Which element provides metadata such as character encoding?
questions.rationale: meta supplies metadata such as charset.

questions.text: Which HTML element preserves whitespace and line breaks as written?
questions.rationale: pre presents preformatted text preserving whitespace.

questions.text: Which element creates an unordered list?
questions.rationale: ul creates a bulleted/unordered list.

questions.text: Which element creates a numbered list?
questions.rationale: ol creates an ordered list.

questions.text: Which pair is used for a definition list entry?
questions.rationale: dt marks the term and dd its description.

questions.text: Which element creates a hyperlink?
questions.rationale: An anchor element with href creates a link.

questions.text: Which attribute specifies the destination of an anchor link?
questions.rationale: href holds the link destination.

questions.text: Which table attribute makes a cell span more than one column?
questions.rationale: colspan specifies the number of columns a cell spans.

questions.text: Which table attribute makes a cell span more than one row?
questions.rationale: rowspan specifies the number of rows a cell spans.

questions.text: Which HTML element contains a row in a table?
questions.rationale: tr represents a table row.

questions.text: Which input type is most suitable when exactly one option in a group should be selected?
questions.rationale: Radio buttons allow one selection per named group.

questions.text: Which control lets a user choose an item from a dropdown list?
questions.rationale: select creates a dropdown/select control.

questions.text: Which part of the CSS rule is the selector in `p { color: blue; }`?
questions.rationale: p selects paragraph elements.

questions.text: Which property changes text colour?
questions.rationale: color sets foreground/text colour.

questions.text: Which property changes the background colour?
questions.rationale: background-color sets the element's background colour.

questions.text: Which CSS selector targets an element with `id="hero"`?
questions.rationale: An ID selector begins with #.

questions.text: Which CSS selector targets all elements with `class="card"`?
questions.rationale: A class selector begins with a dot.

questions.text: Which type of stylesheet is written directly in an element's style attribute?
questions.rationale: An inline style is in the element's style attribute.

questions.text: Which stylesheet type is commonly stored in a separate .css file?
questions.rationale: External CSS is linked from a separate file.

questions.text: Which property sets the thickness of text?
questions.rationale: font-weight controls text weight such as normal or bold.

questions.text: Which property typically controls the text's typeface?
questions.rationale: font-family selects typeface families.

questions.text: Which CSS property rounds the corners of a box?
questions.rationale: border-radius rounds element corners.

questions.text: A user enters example.com and receives the matching IP address before connecting to the site. Which service most directly performs this name resolution?
questions.rationale: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses.

questions.text: A page loads HTML successfully, but a separately linked style file cannot be fetched. Which request/result is most relevant to investigate?

options.label: D
options.text: The stylesheet URL and server response for the CSS resource

questions.rationale: A failed external stylesheet request prevents those styles from loading.

questions.text: A form submits login details over an unencrypted HTTP connection. What is the primary risk?

options.label: A
options.text: Credentials may be exposed in transit

options.label: C
options.text: DNS converts the password into a domain

options.label: D
options.text: The CSS box model stops working

questions.rationale: HTTP alone does not encrypt content in transit.

questions.text: A browser sends web requests, but the app needs reliable, ordered delivery for the data. Which transport is typically appropriate?
questions.rationale: TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream.

questions.text: A real-time service prefers low overhead and can tolerate some packet loss without waiting for retransmission. Which transport may fit?
questions.rationale: UDP avoids TCP's connection and retransmission mechanisms.

questions.text: A user needs to transfer a file to a server using the protocol named in the syllabus. Which choice fits?
questions.rationale: FTP is designed for file transfer.

questions.text: A developer serves the same HTML document over HTTP and HTTPS. What does the HTTPS version add when configured correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: Guaranteed correctness of every page statement

options.label: C
options.text: TLS protection for data exchanged between client and server

questions.rationale: HTTPS uses TLS to protect the connection, not to validate content accuracy.

questions.text: A site owner changes a domain's DNS record but some users still reach the old server temporarily. Which explanation is plausible?

options.label: A
options.text: Cached DNS data may persist until its TTL or cache expires

questions.rationale: Resolvers and clients may cache DNS answers.

questions.text: A site is accessible from a network but not by entering its domain, while a known IP address works. Which issue is worth checking first?
questions.rationale: Success by IP but failure by domain points toward name resolution.

questions.text: A website uses a numeric IPv4 address and a newer 128-bit IPv6 address. Which statement is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: IPv6 is a CSS stylesheet type

options.label: C
options.text: IPv4 uses 128 bits and IPv6 uses 32

options.label: D
options.text: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses; IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses

questions.rationale: IPv4 is 32-bit and IPv6 is 128-bit.

questions.text: A registration form needs a name field, an email field and a submit control. Which HTML approach fits best?

options.label: A
options.text: Create each field as an image

options.label: C
options.text: Use a definition list instead of controls

options.label: D
options.text: Use suitable input types inside a form with a submit button

questions.rationale: Form controls collect input and a submit control sends it.

questions.text: A survey allows a user to select several interests independently. Which control is usually appropriate?

options.label: B
options.text: Radio buttons in one named group

questions.rationale: Checkboxes allow multiple independent selections.

questions.text: A form asks users to select exactly one department from four options. Which is the better choice?

options.label: B
options.text: Radio buttons sharing the same name

questions.rationale: A named radio group allows a single choice.

questions.text: A web form needs a dropdown of department names and a default prompt that is not a valid department. What should the developer do?

options.label: A
options.text: Place the list inside a CSS comment

options.label: B
options.text: Make the options separate h1 elements

options.label: C
options.text: Create a select element with option elements, including a clearly marked prompt option

options.label: D
options.text: Use colspan on the submit button

questions.rationale: select and option represent a dropdown's choices.

questions.text: A data table has a header cell that labels three adjacent columns. Which attribute can help achieve this structure?
questions.rationale: colspan spans columns.

questions.text: A table has one category label that should cover two rows. Which attribute fits?
questions.rationale: rowspan spans rows.

questions.text: A hyperlink to syllabus.html works on one page but fails from a page in a subfolder. What should be checked first?

options.label: D
options.text: The relative path from the current page

questions.rationale: Relative links are resolved from the current document's location.

questions.text: A page must link to a full external website. Which href is generally unambiguous?
questions.rationale: An absolute URL specifies protocol and host.

questions.text: A form's reset control should restore controls to their initial values rather than send the form. Which input type is designed for this?
questions.rationale: type=reset restores initial form control values.

questions.text: Which hidden form field behavior should a developer remember?

options.label: A
options.text: Its value is still submitted and must not be treated as secret merely because it is hidden

options.label: C
options.text: It automatically encrypts all form data

options.label: D
options.text: It is invisible to the server

questions.rationale: Hidden is a presentation/input type, not a security mechanism.

questions.text:
A CSS rule `.notice { color: red; }` is applied to `

`. What does the selector target?

options.label: A
options.text: That paragraph because it has class notice

options.label: B
options.text: All paragraphs only if they lack classes

options.label: C
options.text: Only the element with id notice

questions.rationale: The class selector matches elements carrying that class.

questions.text: A CSS rule `#menu { background: black; }` should apply to the navigation container. Which HTML attribute is needed?
questions.rationale: An ID selector matches the element with id menu.

questions.text: The content box is 200 px wide with 10 px padding on each side and 2 px borders on each side. Under the default content-box model, what is the rendered border-box width, excluding margins?
questions.rationale: Total width = 200 + 20 padding + 4 borders = 224 px.

questions.text: A developer wants a 300 px declared width to include padding and border. Which CSS setting helps?
questions.rationale: border-box includes content, padding and border within the declared size.

questions.text: Which distinction between margin and padding is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Both are always drawn as visible borders

options.label: B
options.text: Margin is outside the border; padding is between content and border

options.label: C
options.text: Padding is outside the element; margin is inside content

options.label: D
options.text: Margin is the text colour; padding is the font

questions.rationale: Margin surrounds the border; padding lies inside it.

questions.text: An external stylesheet is linked but its rules do not appear. Which source-level check is most direct?

options.label: D
options.text: Verify the href path and that the CSS file is successfully served

questions.rationale: The path and response determine whether the stylesheet can load.

questions.text: A developer places a style block in the document head. Which stylesheet type is this?
questions.rationale: A style element in the HTML document is internal/embedded CSS.

questions.text: A developer applies `color: blue` in an element's style attribute. Which category is this?
questions.rationale: The style attribute is inline CSS.

questions.text: Which selector matches every paragraph inside a section, including deeper nested paragraphs?
questions.rationale: The descendant selector includes nested descendants.

questions.text: Which selector matches only paragraph elements that are direct children of a section?
questions.rationale: The child combinator > selects direct children only.

questions.text: A card needs a soft shadow, rounded corners and a subtle background gradient. Which combination directly supports those effects?
questions.rationale: Those CSS features respectively add shadows, rounded corners and gradients.

questions.text: A tooltip should appear when a user hovers over an element. Which CSS concept can support this behavior?

options.label: C
options.text: A :hover selector with a styled tooltip element

questions.rationale: The :hover pseudo-class can reveal or style a tooltip.

questions.text: An icon should rotate without changing its place in normal document flow. Which CSS feature is designed for that visual effect?
questions.rationale: Transforms apply visual rotations and other transformations.

questions.text: A small animation should progress through defined stages over time. Which CSS feature is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Keyframes describe stages used by CSS animations.

questions.text: A navigation menu should remain positioned relative to its normal place, with a small offset. Which positioning mode best fits?

options.label: D
options.text: absolute with no positioned ancestor always

questions.rationale: Relative positioning offsets an element from its normal position.

questions.text: A floating help control should stay at the same viewport location as the page scrolls. Which positioning mode fits?
questions.rationale: Fixed positioning is relative to the viewport.

questions.text: A badge should be positioned relative to a card whose position is set to relative. Which mode is commonly used for the badge?
questions.rationale: An absolutely positioned child can be placed relative to the positioned card.

questions.text: A developer uses one linked CSS file for ten HTML pages. What is the main maintenance benefit?

options.label: B
options.text: Every page automatically gets a unique domain

options.label: C
options.text: HTML validation is no longer needed

options.label: D
options.text: A single stylesheet can update shared presentation across all pages

questions.rationale: Shared external CSS centralizes common styling.

questions.text: A title is styled by `h1 { color: black; }` and `.hero { color: teal; }`, and the title has class hero. Assuming equal origin and no !important, which colour applies?

options.label: A
options.text: teal because a class selector is more specific than a type selector

options.label: B
options.text: black because type selectors always win

options.label: D
options.text: Neither rule can match an h1

questions.rationale: A class selector has greater specificity than a type selector.

questions.text: A webpage should animate an element while respecting a design that avoids sudden motion for users who request reduced motion. Which approach is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace animation with repeated blinking text

options.label: C
options.text: Use a reduced-motion media query to reduce/disable nonessential animation

questions.rationale: prefers-reduced-motion allows adaptation for motion sensitivity.

questions.text: A browser can resolve a domain to an IP address, but the server returns an HTTP 404 for `/courses/sem1.html`. What is the most targeted interpretation?

options.label: A
options.text: The network has no IP connectivity

options.label: C
options.text: Name resolution and server contact worked; the requested resource path was not found

questions.rationale: A 404 means the server was reached but did not find the requested resource.

questions.text: A site opens on HTTPS, but browser requests for images still use HTTP. What is the main issue to address?

options.label: A
options.text: Change all img tags to table tags

options.label: B
options.text: Replace IPv6 with an HTML selector

options.label: C
options.text: Use UDP to style the image

options.label: D
options.text: Mixed content: serve the image resources securely too

questions.rationale: HTTP subresources on an HTTPS page can create mixed-content warnings or be blocked.

questions.text: A client uploads files reliably but slowly because the transfer must recover lost data and preserve order. Which protocol comparison is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: TCP provides reliable ordered transport; UDP does not guarantee delivery/order

options.label: B
options.text: HTTP is a CSS style type

options.label: C
options.text: FTP is the IP address version

options.label: D
options.text: UDP guarantees every packet is delivered in order

questions.rationale: TCP provides reliability and ordering; UDP offers no such guarantee by itself.

questions.text: A website is moved from one IP address to another. The domain still resolves to the old address for some users. Which pair of actions is most relevant?

options.label: B
options.text: Update the appropriate DNS record and account for caching/TTL propagation

options.label: C
options.text: Change the CSS ID selector and refresh font-weight

options.label: D
options.text: Rename the homepage from h1 to h2

questions.rationale: DNS update and cache expiry explain the transition.

questions.text: A developer makes a login page with HTTPS, but the server stores passwords as plain text. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: HTTPS automatically encrypts the database at rest

options.label: B
options.text: Plain-text storage is safe because the form is hidden

options.label: C
options.text: CSS can replace password storage controls

options.label: D
options.text: HTTPS protects data in transit; it does not by itself secure how the server stores passwords

questions.rationale: Transport encryption does not provide a secure password-storage design.

questions.text: A developer must choose between TCP and UDP for a file upload requiring complete, ordered data. Which choice best fits and why?

options.label: A
options.text: CSS, because it handles file transfer

options.label: B
options.text: TCP, because it supplies reliability and ordered delivery

options.label: D
options.text: UDP, because it guarantees retransmission by default

questions.rationale: A complete ordered transfer typically needs TCP or an application-level equivalent.

questions.text: A site uses an IP address in a link instead of a domain. Which maintenance disadvantage is most plausible?

options.label: A
options.text: HTTPS no longer works with domains

options.label: B
options.text: An IP address is always encrypted

options.label: C
options.text: The link must change if the service's address changes, while a stable domain can be repointed via DNS

options.label: D
options.text: A domain name cannot resolve to an IP

questions.rationale: A stable domain decouples a user-facing name from a server address.

questions.text: An HTML page loads but the external CSS file returns 403 Forbidden. What should be checked before rewriting every selector?

options.label: A
options.text: The stylesheet resource's permissions/access rules and requested path

options.label: C
options.text: Whether the page has a radio button

questions.rationale: 403 indicates the server understood the request but refused access.

questions.text: A domain resolves correctly and the web server responds, but HTTPS warns that the certificate is for a different hostname. What should be investigated?
questions.rationale: A hostname mismatch is a certificate/TLS configuration issue.

questions.text: A page needs a live feed where occasional dropped packets are acceptable and low latency matters more than guaranteed transport delivery. Which transport is a plausible choice?
questions.rationale: UDP may fit latency-sensitive communication tolerant of packet loss.

questions.text: A card has width: 240px, padding: 12px on both sides and border: 3px on both sides under content-box sizing. Without margins, what is its outer width?
questions.rationale: 240 + 24 padding + 6 border = 270 px.

questions.text: An element has `position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: 0;`. Which ancestor most directly determines its positioning reference when that ancestor is positioned?

options.label: B
options.text: The nearest paragraph regardless of positioning

questions.rationale: Absolutely positioned elements use their nearest positioned ancestor as containing block in common layouts.

questions.text: A class selector and an ID selector both set the same property on an element, with equal origin and no !important. Which usually wins?

options.label: B
options.text: The ID selector due to higher specificity

options.label: D
options.text: The later HTML tag name regardless of CSS order

questions.rationale: ID selectors have greater specificity than class selectors.

questions.text: A layout must remain in the normal document flow and shift 8 px down from where it would normally appear. Which setting most directly fits?

options.label: B
options.text: position: absolute; top: 8px with no containing block

questions.rationale: Relative positioning keeps the element's original layout space.

questions.text: A developer sets an image width and height to fixed dimensions but aspect ratio becomes distorted. What is a sensible correction?

options.label: A
options.text: Set one dimension and preserve the intrinsic aspect ratio, or use an appropriate object-fit behavior

options.label: B
options.text: Add a colspan attribute to the image

options.label: D
options.text: Use font-weight to restore the image shape

questions.rationale: Preserving aspect ratio or choosing object-fit avoids unintended stretching.

questions.text: A CSS background gradient is visible, but text contrast is poor on part of the card. What is the best fix?

options.label: A
options.text: Set the HTML title to the same colour

options.label: C
options.text: Adjust the gradient/overlay or text colour to maintain readable contrast across the background

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the background with a hyperlink

questions.rationale: Contrast must be adequate throughout the text area.

questions.text: A tooltip is clipped inside a container that has overflow hidden. What should be inspected?

options.label: D
options.text: The containing element's overflow/positioning and the tooltip's placement in the layout

questions.rationale: Overflow and containing-block geometry can clip positioned tooltips.

questions.text: A site requires animations to run only when reduced motion is not requested. Which CSS organization best meets that constraint?

options.label: A
options.text: Use an HTML meta tag to force motion

options.label: B
options.text: Define the animation as default and disable/reduce it under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce

options.label: C
options.text: Use DNS caching to control animation

options.label: D
options.text: Set every animation to infinite blink

questions.rationale: A reduced-motion media query can disable nonessential animation.

questions.text: External CSS is linked correctly, but inline style sets a different color on one element. Which explanation commonly applies?

options.label: A
options.text: The element becomes an HTML comment

options.label: B
options.text: External CSS always beats inline styles

options.label: C
options.text: The inline style generally has higher priority than a normal author stylesheet rule for the same property

options.label: D
options.text: The browser blends the two colours

questions.rationale: Inline author styles usually take priority over ordinary author stylesheet declarations.

questions.text: An absolutely positioned menu overlays a button and intercepts its clicks. Which CSS concept may help control which item appears above the other?
questions.rationale: z-index controls stacking order in applicable stacking contexts.

questions.text: A registration form lets users select multiple skills and one experience level. Which control design respects both requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Checkboxes for skills and a single named radio group for experience level

options.label: B
options.text: A hidden input for every visible choice

options.label: C
options.text: A submit button for each skill

options.label: D
options.text: One radio group for every skill and multiple levels

questions.rationale: Checkboxes allow multiple independent choices; radio groups enforce one choice.

questions.text: A table header must label two columns, while a category heading spans two body rows. Which attributes serve those needs, respectively?
questions.rationale: colspan spans columns; rowspan spans rows.

questions.text: A stylesheet change unexpectedly affects every paragraph on a site. Which selector is most likely responsible?

options.label: A
options.text: An ID selector used on one element

options.label: B
options.text: An inline style attribute on a single element

options.label: C
options.text: A broad type selector `p` in a shared external stylesheet

options.label: D
options.text: A fragment identifier in one hyperlink

questions.rationale: A shared type selector matches all paragraph elements in its scope.

questions.text: A form submission loses the selected department. All radio inputs have different `name` attributes. What is the most likely markup-level issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The page uses an HTML5 doctype

options.label: C
options.text: The CSS background is a gradient

options.label: D
options.text: The radio controls are not grouped under the same name, so their values are submitted as separate fields

questions.rationale: Radio groups use the same name to represent a single-choice field.

questions.text: A page has a button that should submit a form, but clicking it resets the inputs. Which attribute value should be checked?

options.label: B
options.text: The button/input type may be reset instead of submit

options.label: C
options.text: The anchor href must be a CSS class

questions.rationale: A reset control restores initial values rather than submitting.

questions.text: A link works when the page is at `/index.html`, but not when the same code is moved to `/students/index.html`. It uses `href="syllabus.html"`. Why?

options.label: A
options.text: The link's text must be a heading

options.label: B
options.text: The browser no longer supports anchors

options.label: C
options.text: The destination needs a row span

options.label: D
options.text: The relative URL now resolves under `/students/`, so the path must be updated for the new location

questions.rationale: Relative links are resolved from the current document path.

questions.text: An inline style, an ID rule and a class rule disagree on the same text colour. Which sequence should guide diagnosis before changing values?

options.label: A
options.text: Check importance/origin, specificity and then source order for applicable declarations

options.label: D
options.text: Choose the longest selector without inspecting the cascade

questions.rationale: The cascade considers origin/importance, specificity and source order.

questions.text: A developer places a tooltip beside a button using absolute positioning. It appears in the wrong place after layout changes. Which design change may make the placement more predictable?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the button with a table footer

options.label: B
options.text: Move the tooltip text into the DNS record

options.label: C
options.text: Give a suitable containing wrapper relative positioning and position the tooltip within it

questions.rationale: A positioned wrapper creates a predictable containing block.

questions.text: A page uses CSS animation on a decorative element and notices excessive movement for some users. What is the most appropriate improvement?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase movement until it becomes familiar

options.label: C
options.text: Make animation mandatory in the HTML structure

options.label: D
options.text: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and provide a reduced-motion or no-animation state

questions.rationale: Users' reduced-motion preferences should be respected.

questions.text: A developer is asked to make a static page containing a heading, paragraph, image with alternative text, list and working links. Which review catches the most important structural problems before styling?

options.label: B
options.text: Check semantic elements, valid nesting, required attributes and correct link/image paths

questions.rationale: Correct structure and valid resources matter before visual polish.

questions.text: A site loads HTML and images, but not CSS; the CSS URL returns 404. What should be done first?

options.label: B
options.text: Correct the link/path or restore the stylesheet at the requested URL, then retest the page

options.label: C
options.text: Rewrite every CSS rule without checking the URL

questions.rationale: A 404 for the stylesheet means the resource path or file is unavailable.

questions.text: A form needs one department choice and multiple interests; submitted values should be meaningful. Which combined setup is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Use unnamed radio inputs for everything

options.label: B
options.text: Use a single hidden field and no visible controls

options.label: C
options.text: Use a named radio group for department, named checkboxes for interests and a submit control

options.label: D
options.text: Use table cells without a form

questions.rationale: Names provide submitted field keys and controls reflect single/multiple selection.

questions.text: A page must fit a card within a 300 px border-box width including 20 px padding on each side and 2 px borders. With `box-sizing: border-box`, what content width remains?
questions.rationale: Content width = 300 − 40 padding − 4 borders = 256 px.

questions.text: An external stylesheet sets a heading teal, but a normal class rule changes it to purple and an ID rule changes it to navy. With equal origin/importance, which usually wins?

options.label: A
options.text: The ID rule, because it has higher specificity

options.label: B
options.text: The browser picks the first colour alphabetically

options.label: C
options.text: The type selector, because it is external

options.label: D
options.text: The class rule always beats an ID

questions.rationale: ID specificity exceeds class and type specificity.

questions.text: A page uses HTTPS but loads a third-party image with an HTTP URL. What is the best correction?

options.label: B
options.text: Switch DNS from IPv4 to CSS

options.label: C
options.text: Use an HTTPS image endpoint or another secure resource source

options.label: D
options.text: Put the image URL in a hidden input

questions.rationale: Securely load subresources to avoid mixed content.

questions.text: A web server accepts requests by IP but a public domain fails after a deployment. The server logs show no request for the domain. Which path is most worth checking first?

options.label: A
options.text: DNS records/propagation and client resolver cache

questions.rationale: If requests never reach the server via the domain, name resolution is a primary suspect.

questions.text: A developer creates a horizontal navigation bar and wants it to wrap on small screens while retaining a clear layout. Which approach is most suitable?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a meta title to space items

options.label: B
options.text: Use flexible layout rules such as flexbox with wrapping and appropriate spacing

options.label: C
options.text: Position every item at a fixed viewport coordinate

options.label: D
options.text: Make every link a background image

questions.rationale: Flexible layout handles variable widths better than fixed coordinates.

questions.text: An element must animate into view, but should not create a large movement for users who opt out of animation. What is the complete solution?

options.label: B
options.text: Place animation instructions in alt text

options.label: C
options.text: Use absolute positioning without considering user preference

options.label: D
options.text: Use CSS animation/transform for the normal case and a reduced-motion media query to simplify or disable it

questions.rationale: Motion styling and accessibility preference can be handled together.

questions.text: A site has duplicate IDs because the same `id="menu"` is applied to every navigation item. What change is appropriate if they share the same styling?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a class for the repeated items and reserve IDs for unique elements

options.label: D
options.text: Keep all duplicate IDs because they improve specificity

questions.rationale: Classes are suitable for repeated groups; IDs should uniquely identify an element.

questions.text: A developer must deliver a linked external CSS file and a semantic HTML page. Which verification set is most complete?

options.label: A
options.text: Confirm only the domain name and stop

options.label: C
options.text: Confirm stylesheet link/path, inspect loaded styles, validate element nesting and test links/image alt text at target sizes

questions.rationale: Resource loading, structure, links and accessibility-relevant attributes are all essential.
